deep.reconstruction:
Folio 19r is the title page and opening paragraph of Riemann's student essay 'Versuch einer allgemeinen[eren] Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation' (dated January 1847). It was published posthumously in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (1876, ed. Weber with Dedekind) as item XIX. The page contains no formulas or derivations. It only states the programme.

Goal: define an operator that sends a function z(x) to a new function of the same variable. The relation between the two is governed by a single number nu, which may be fractional. The construction must satisfy three conditions:
- For integer nu > 0 the result is the nu-th derivative d^nu z/dx^nu.
- For integer nu < 0 it is the |nu|-fold integral.
- For nu = 0 it is z itself.

In modern terms Riemann asks for a one-parameter family of operators D^nu that interpolates the integer-order derivatives and repeated integrals.

Methodological remark: the results of ordinary differential and integral calculus are presupposed. Riemann explicitly refuses to simply extend to fractional orders the rules valid for all integer orders, such as D^m D^n = D^(m+n). Instead those results serve only two purposes: (a) to justify the procedure, and (b) as a 'Wegweiser' (heuristic guide) for finding it.

The next page carries out the heuristic. It does not use the recursive definition of derivatives. It uses an 'independent' characterisation: D^n z equals n! times the coefficient of h^n in the Taylor expansion z(x+h) = sum_p z^(p)(x) h^p / p!.

Later in the essay (not on this page) Riemann reaches his generalised operator. It is the integral (1/Gamma(nu)) * integral_k^x (x-t)^(nu-1) z(t) dt plus a complementary function. This is the modern Riemann–Liouville fractional integral.

Nothing on this page needs filling in by me.
errors: No mathematical errors: the page is purely programmatic.

Interpretive point, not an error: the requirement that integer negative orders agree with 'the integrals' is not well defined without fixing a base point or constants of integration. Riemann's later treatment handles this with an arbitrary lower limit and a complementary function, which is a known weak point of the essay.

results.what: Programme of defining differentiation/integration of arbitrary (fractional) order nu, interpolating integer-order derivatives (nu>0), repeated integrals (nu<0) and the identity (nu=0)
results.usually_credited_to: Leibniz (1695 letter to L'Hôpital), Euler, Lacroix, Fourier, Abel (1823), Liouville (1832-37); Riemann's version from this 1847 essay (published 1876); Riemann–Liouville operator named jointly

results.what: Methodological stance: derive the generalisation from an independent (Taylor-coefficient) characterisation of derivatives rather than by extending integer-order rules
results.modern_name: Interpolation of the sequence of derivatives via Taylor coefficients / generalised Taylor series

deep.surprise_reason: This is the opening page of a well-known, published (Werke 1876) student essay of Riemann, which is the origin of the 'Riemann' in Riemann–Liouville fractional integral. The page contains only the statement of aims, with no new mathematics.

checkable.asserts: Context, not on this page. The generalised power rule D^nu x^a = Gamma(a+1)/Gamma(a+1-nu) x^(a-nu) agrees with ordinary differentiation for integer nu=n.
Context, not on this page. Cauchy's repeated-integral formula: for nu=3 the Riemann–Liouville integral equals the threefold iterated integral, the 'integer negative order' case of the programme.
Context, not on this page. The half-derivative of x is Gamma(2)/Gamma(3/2) x^(1/2) = 2 sqrt(x/pi). Here we only check Gamma(3/2) = sqrt(pi)/2, the constant involved.

transcription_corrections: Title: the published Werke title reads 'Versuch einer allgemeinen Auffassung der Integration und Differentiation'. The manuscript reading 'allgemeineren' is plausible from the image but should be checked against the hand.
'Riemann 7' at top right is a later archival/pencil label, not part of the text. The '79' in the right margin is a later foliation/page number.
Rest of the transcription matches the image ('kön-ne', 'ausdrü-cken läßt', 'bezüglich', 'Wegweiser dienen, dasselbe zu finden').
